item.title: Election fever, Dangote Refinery to drive stock investors’ fortune at year end
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Nigerian stock market is projected to cross the N200 trillion market capitalisation by December 2026, while investors’ returns could exceed 57 per cent. Capital market analysts, who made the projections, said the anticipated listing of shares of Dangote Petroleum Refinery on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), coupled with improved investor confidence, strong corporate earnings, increased market liquidity and favourable macroeconomic developments, would provide further impetus for the equities market. They also projected that the NGX All-Share Index (ASI), the market’s major performance indicator, could close the year at about 280,000 points. However, some analysts have warned that profit-taking, election-related uncertainties and global economic developments could trigger intermittent volatility. But the analysts agreed that the concern over 2027 general election is around possible policy change adding that if there are no major adverse economic policy developments capable of undermining investor confidence the impact of the election would be less severe. Market performance so far A review of the market’s performance Year-to-Date, YtD, as at last week, showed that investors’ wealth had increased by N62.76 trillion, representing a 60.47 per cent appreciation. Market capitalisation, which measures the total value of listed equities, rose from N99.376 trillion at the beginning of the year to N162.134 trillion last week. Similarly, the NGX ASI appreciated by 60.5 per cent, rising from 155,613.03 points at the beginning of the year to 249,710.59 points. The impressive performance has been supported by relative stability in the foreign exchange market, renewed investor confidence, strong corporate earnings, easing inflation, improved liquidity in the financial system and the decision of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to reduce the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to 23 per cent. Analysts’ projections Speaking to Financial Vanguard on his projection for the year-end, Olatunde Amolegbe, immediate past President, Chartered Institute of Stockbrokers (CIS), and Managing Director, Arthur Stevens Asset Management Limited, said he remained cautiously optimistic about the equities market. He stated: “I remain cautiously optimistic about the Nigerian stock market for the rest of the year. My expectation is that the All-Share Index will deliver a full-year return of approximately 57.65%. “Although the market has recorded impressive gains so far, I expect some moderation in the coming weeks, as investors may take profits following the significant rally we have witnessed. We could also see some volatility as investors reposition their portfolios ahead of the new year. “On the positive side, relatively strong corporate earnings, improved investor confidence, increased domestic participation and ongoing economic reforms should continue to provide support for the market. item.description: By Efe Onodjae LAGOS — THE Lagos State governorship candidates of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Dr Obafemi Hamzat; African Democratic Congress, ADC, Mr Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour; Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Funso Doherty and Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Mr Adedeji Doherty, yesterday, unveiled their development plans for housing, traffic congestion, transportation, security and infrastructure if elected in 2027. Read Also: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal They presented their credentials, policy proposals and vision for the state ahead of the governorship election. The candidates spoke at a debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, which comprises Vanguard Newspaper, Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper and The Cable. During the debate, the candidates outlined different approaches to addressing the developmental challenges facing Lagos. On the developmental challenges facing the state, the APC candidate, Dr Hamzat, emphasised continuity and expansion of existing infrastructure, while the ADC candidate, Mr Rhodes-Vivour, called for a departure from what he described as two decades of bad governance. In his remarks, the NDC candidate, Mr Doherty, questioned the political interests surrounding the state’s public transportation system, alleging that the failure to modernise the sector was deliberate. Taming traffic in Lagos On traffic congestion, Doherty alleged that the persistent gridlock in Lagos was being sustained by vested interests benefiting from the existing chaotic public transportation system. He argued that the state’s traffic problems were not simply the result of inadequate infrastructure but also reflected poor management of existing roads and the failure to modernise public transportation. The NDC candidate also alluded to the informal transport network popularly associated with agberos, arguing that the interests surrounding the system had made its modernisation politically difficult. He said: “Lagos continues to rely on dilapidated commercial buses operating chaotically, contributing to gridlock and making commuting difficult for residents. “Our public transportation system is not modernised. Thousands of rickety buses are moving around. We must ask ourselves: are these what our people deserve? Why has it taken so long to modernise public transportation? “In my opinion, the lack of modern transportation is not by accident. There are vested interests in operating the bus system the way it is. Many of us understand the agbero system; there is an ecosystem around it, and there is no political will to deal with that problem.” “We would modernise public transportation because we would be elected by the people and not by the agbero network,” he added. item.title: INEC in Eye of the Storm: Electoral body battles to clean voters’ register – Investigation
item.description: By Jide Ajani There is perhaps no greater threat to electoral integrity than an unreliable Voters’ Register. Before the first ballot is cast or the first result announced, the credibility of an election is already being determined by the document that establishes who is entitled to vote. Read Also: * Explainer: Who won 2023 presidential 2023 in Kaduna, Katsina – the 161,829 votes difference * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal The Voters’ Register is the foundation of the electoral process. It defines the electorate, determines the numerical strength of constituencies and provides the basis for accreditation and voting. It is, fundamentally, the official record of a people’s democratic membership. Yet, in Nigeria, its credibility remains a persistent source of anxiety. The historical paradox: have we really progressed? Nigeria has travelled a considerable distance from the largely manual registration arrangements of the 1950s to biometric registration, electronic databases and the deployment of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). The 1959 general election, conducted under the Electoral Commission of Nigeria (ECN), had approximately nine million registered voters. Subsequent elections in 1964/65, 1979, 1983 and 1993 exposed different administrative and political challenges associated with voter registration. 4th Republic The Fourth Republic introduced more sophisticated systems, including permanent voter cards, biometric identification and mechanisms for detecting duplicate registrations. Yet technological advancement has not necessarily translated into greater electoral credibility. A bigger register is not automatically a better register. A digital register is not necessarily reliable, and biometric technology is not beyond manipulation. Consider the fluctuations in registration figures: 73.5 million in 2011, 67.4 million in 2015 and approximately 84 million in 2019. Such changes do not establish manipulation, since legitimate deletions and corrections occur The real test is fidelity: whether the names represent living, eligible citizens entitled to vote, or whether they are mere AI-generated entities. INEC and the collapse of public confidence An electoral commission’s credibility rests not merely on constitutional independence but on demonstrable impartiality, competence and transparency. Constitutional independence in itself does not guarantee operational independence when the personnel saddled with responsibilities decide to go rogue on the system. When public confidence in INEC declines, virtually every administrative decision becomes vulnerable to suspicion, from voter registration and PVC distribution to accreditation and results management. This is the distinction between administrative validity and democratic legitimacy. item.title: Bandits burn 12 family members
item.description: Twelve members of the same family have been killed after armed bandits set their residence ablaze during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. Seven other residents were also abducted during the attack, which occurred on Saturday night in Dosara Birnin Kaya Ward, despite efforts by the community to alert security agencies. This is coming barely one week after bandits ambushed security personnel at Gidan Kano along the Gusau-Sokoto highway within the same local government and killed five policemen. A resident, who spoke to Daily Trust on condition of anonymity, said the attackers invaded the residence of one Mallam Muhammadu Sani at about 10 pm. 1 killed in NDC rally as attacks rise Middle Belt leaders’ visit to Tinubu raises unity questions He said 13 members of the family were trapped inside a room after locking themselves in to escape being abducted by the attackers. According to him, those inside the room included Sani, his two wives and their six children, as well as the wife of his younger brother and their three children. He said the bandits ordered the occupants to open the door, but when they refused, the attackers set the room ablaze. Only the wife of Sani’s younger brother reportedly escaped, while the remaining 12 occupants died from the intense heat and fire. The resident said the community immediately contacted the Maradun Local Government Chairman, Sanusi Ahmed Dosara, who made efforts to reach security formations for assistance. However, he said the security agencies could not intervene before the tragedy occurred. “We informed the local government chairman, Dosara, and he tried all he could to reach the security personnel. He told us he had spoken with different security formations, but nobody came to our rescue,” he said. He expressed disappointment that no security personnel responded to their distress calls despite the village’s proximity to Maradun town, where military and police formations are located. “Imagine, the distance between our village and Dosara is just about half a kilometre, while from Dosara to Maradun is about one kilometre. In total, it is just about one and a half kilometres between our village and the local government headquarters. “There is a military base in Maradun, a mobile police base and a police headquarters, yet none of them came to our aid until the bandits burnt the 12 people alive,” he said. Another resident confirmed that seven other people were abducted during the attack and remained in the custody of the bandits as of the time he spoke to Daily Trust. He appealed to security agencies to strengthen their presence in the area and take urgent measures to protect residents against further attacks. item.title: Zuba fruit market traders decry poor access road
item.description: Some traders at Zuba Fruit Market, Federal Capital Territory (FCT), have decried the poor access road, saying it disrupts business activities, discourages customers and increases transportation costs. They spoke in separate interviews with the News Agency of Nigeria on Wednesday in Abuja. They said the road, which had deteriorated over time, becomes almost impassable during the rainy season due to deep potholes, muddy sections and poor drainage. According to them, the poor condition of the road discourages customers from visiting the market and causes delays in transporting fresh fruits and vegetables. A fruit wholesaler, Mr Mohammed Usman, said many commercial vehicles avoided the road because of its poor state, forcing traders to pay higher transport fares. “The bad road has affected our business seriously. Many transporters charge extra because they fear damage to their vehicles. “Some customers also turn back when they see the condition of the road, while others prefer buying from markets with easier access,” he said. Another trader, Mr Augustine Igwe, said vehicles conveying fruits from farms frequently developed mechanical faults due to the poor condition of the road. One of the bad roads in Zuba “We spend more money repairing our vehicles and paying higher transport fares. These costs eventually increase the prices of fruits. “Sometimes, vehicles carrying fruits get stuck, leading to delays and spoilage of some produce. The extra cost is eventually passed on to buyers,” he said. A buyer, Mrs Esther Okoli, described the road as a major challenge, especially for elderly people and parents visiting the market with children. “The road is in a terrible state. Many customers complain before coming here, while transporters charge us more because of the bad road. “Whenever it rains, the road becomes almost impassable because of stagnant water and deep potholes. Carrying goods through such conditions is stressful,” she said. Another buyer, Mr Emmanuel Johnson, said the poor condition of the road increased the cost and difficulty of moving goods from the market. “I shop here for affordable prices, but the poor road discourages buyers. Commercial vehicles often avoid the market, forcing us to carry purchases over long distances. ”A commercial driver, Mr Abdullahi Ibrahim, said frequent use of the road increased vehicle maintenance costs due to damaged tyres and suspension systems. He appealed to the FCT Administration to prioritise the rehabilitation of the access road to improve transportation and support businesses operating in the market. NAN reports that Zuba Fruit Market supplies fruits and vegetables daily, serving thousands of consumers within the FCT and neighbouring communities. The traders and buyers expressed optimism that prompt government intervention would improve access to the market, reduce transportation costs and enhance economic activities in the area.(NAN)

item.title: 2027: APC chieftain laments 73% voter apathy in Aramoko
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and member of the President Bola Tinubu/APC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, Engineer Atinuke Owolabi, has expressed concern over the low voter turnout in Aramoko-Ekiti during the 2023 presidential election, saying about 73 per cent of registered voters in the community did not participate. Owolabi, who is also the convener of PBAT-MOB Aramoko Community Engagement, spoke during an APC voter education exercise and community engagement in Aramoko, Ekiti Central Senatorial District, over the weekend. The programme, organised in support of the re-election bids of President Tinubu and Senate Leader, Senator Michael Opeyemi Bamidele, was held under the theme, “My Vote, My Voice”. She also represents the South-West as a member of the North Central Development Commission. Owolabi said voter education was essential to strengthening democracy, particularly in rural communities where inadequate information about electoral procedures could discourage participation or lead to invalid votes. Presenting figures from the 2023 presidential election, she said Ekiti State had 988,923 registered voters, out of whom 315,058 were accredited, while 308,171 valid votes were recorded and 6,301 ballots were rejected. She said available ward-level records for Aramoko I and Aramoko II showed a combined 17,426 registered voters, compared with 4,680 votes reportedly cast during the presidential election. According to her, the figures indicated that approximately 12,746 registered voters did not participate, representing about 73 per cent of the electorate in the two wards. She urged residents to improve their participation in future elections, stressing the need for the community to translate its voting strength into meaningful democratic engagement. Owolabi said the exercise was designed to educate residents on voting procedures, encourage participation and reduce the number of rejected ballots. The programme also featured the unveiling of a voter education handbook intended to guide residents on electoral processes, identification of polling units and the proper use of their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). She said: “I believe voter education is key. If we cannot completely eliminate rejected votes, we should at least be able to reduce them in Ekiti State, particularly in Aramoko, my community. “We are here to sensitise our people on the correct way to vote. When they go to the polling units, they must ensure that they vote correctly. “We have the population, and we have the voters. What is really lacking is adequate information. Our people need to understand the right way to vote. “Today, we have unveiled a voter education handbook, which is a welcome development. Through this handbook, our people will be taught what elections are all about. item.title: Aba South establishes commercial farms to boost revenue, create jobs
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Aba South Local Government Area of Abia State has established commercial poultry and piggery farms as part of efforts to boost its internally generated revenue (IGR), create jobs and equip residents with skills in animal husbandry. The Executive Chairman of the council, Chief Obialo Anyanwu, disclosed this while briefing journalists on his administration’s two-year achievements, explaining that the initiative was aimed at making the local government more financially self-reliant. Anyanwu said his administration was exploring sustainable revenue sources to strengthen the council’s capacity to deliver services rather than depend entirely on external funding. He explained that the farms would also serve as training centres where residents would acquire practical skills in animal farming, enabling them to establish their own businesses and employ others. He said: “We don’t believe in all these 10kg of rice empowerment. What we want in Aba South is giving our people that level of empowerment that will make them self-sustaining and employ others. So, we’ll teach the techniques needed to succeed in the business. “The three buildings in the poultry section are up, two are already roofed, and the staff quarters are at the lintel stage because it’s a proper farm and people must reside there. “Possibly by the end of the year, everything will take off. So, we’re envisaging such a future. We, as the third tier of government, must stand for ourselves, and it has pushed us into doing commercial poultry and commercial pig farming.” The chairman disclosed that the poultry farm occupies 14 plots of land, while the piggery farm covers seven plots. He added that the projects would generate revenue for the council, create employment opportunities and provide practical agricultural training for residents, including staff of the council’s agriculture department. On healthcare, Anyanwu said the council had established and equipped 22 Glycoster World Primary Healthcare Centres in partnership with the Abia State Government. He said the facilities had been commissioned and made operational, adding that the council had also organised free medical tests and treatments for residents. On education, the chairman said the council was supporting Governor Alex Otti’s free back-to-school programme through the distribution of 4,000 school bags to pupils in primary schools across the local government area. He explained that the initial target was 10,000 beneficiaries but that the distribution would be carried out in phases after an enumeration exercise showed that the number of eligible pupils exceeded the target. Anyanwu also disclosed that the council was partnering with the state government on primary school development, including the ongoing construction of a smart school along Etche Road. item.title: Trump admits his mass deportation policy was ‘too tough’
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that his mass deportation of undocumented immigrants was “too tough,” according to an excerpt of an interview with CBS aired Sunday. Asked about his deportation policy, Trump told CBS’ “60 Minutes”: “I think it was too tough…I think it might be too tough.” The excerpt was published by CBS on X ahead of a broadcast of the interview on network TV later Sunday. It was recorded after the Republican Party’s heavy loss in midterm elections on Tuesday. While Trump has won some domestic support for securing the US southern border, his administration’s aggressive push to deport millions of undocumented migrants has drawn widespread criticism. However, Trump on Friday appointed the architect of that hardline policy, Stephen Miller, as his chief of staff on Friday, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback after the Republican election loss. Miller has been synonymous with scenes of masked immigration agents committing violence after he backed federal agents who shot and killed two Americans early this year. item.title: Sultan directs Muslims to sight Jumada Assaniya moon Monday
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO – The Sultanate Council of Sokoto has called on Muslims across Nigeria to search for the new crescent moon of Jumada Assaniya 1448AH on Monday, November 9, 2026. The directive was contained in a statement dated November 8, 2026, signed by Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu and made available to journalists on Sunday. According to the statement, the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council identified Monday as the 29th day of Jumada al-Ula 1448AH and the appropriate date for the nationwide moon-sighting exercise. The council urged Muslims across the country to actively participate in the exercise by looking out for the new crescent moon after sunset on Monday. It specifically requested anyone who sights the crescent to promptly report the observation to the nearest District or Village Head for onward transmission to His Eminence, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, CFR, mni, the Sultan of Sokoto and President-General of the Nigeria Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA). The council stressed the importance of timely and credible reports of confirmed sightings to enable the Sultan to make the appropriate religious announcement on the commencement of the new Islamic month. It noted that the Sultan remains the recognised authority responsible for communicating the outcome of the moon-sighting exercise to Muslims across the country. The announcement underscores the role of the Sultanate Council in coordinating Islamic religious affairs and guiding the Muslim Ummah on matters concerning the Islamic lunar calendar. In a prayer, Professor Sambo Wali Junaidu, Waziri and Chairman of the Advisory Committee on Religious Affairs of the Sultanate Council, asked Allah (SWT) to grant Muslims the guidance and strength to discharge the religious responsibility successfully. The council also prayed for divine assistance and acceptance of the exercise, urging Muslims to approach the assignment with sincerity, vigilance and a strong sense of religious commitment. item.title: Fermin brace earns Liga leaders Barcelona 2-1 win at Atletico
item.description: Fermin Lopez struck twice to help Barcelona come from behind to beat Atletico Madrid 2-1 and move three points clear at the top of La Liga. The Spanish champions lead second place Real Madrid, who beat Valencia 3-0 on Saturday, with Atletico third, now five points behind. Giuliano Simeone fired Atletico ahead in a high-octane start, before Lopez pulled Barca level shortly before the interval at the Metropolitano stadium. The 23-year-old Spain international netted the winner after 66 minutes when Lamine Yamal slipped him in. The match started at a fast pace and both teams hit the woodwork in the opening stages. Alvarez, who tried and failed to force a move from Atletico to Barca in the summer, rounded goalkeeper Joan Garcia but could not finish off the chance as the defence blocked his route to goal. From the resulting corner Atletico defender Marc Pubill headed against the crossbar with Garcia beaten. At the other end Pedri crashed a strike against the woodwork after being fed by Barca’s teenage star Lamine Yamal. Atletico took the lead in the 10th minute, slicing Barca’s defence open. Alvarez crossed for Giuliano Simeone to turn home from close range. The game settled down after that pulsating start, although Alvarez came close to scoring Atletico’s second. The Argentine international’s shot was fumbled by Garcia, but the goalkeeper was able to collect the ball quickly afterwards. Yamal blasted into the side-netting from a tight angle with Barcelona not able to click into their top gears. Despite their struggles they went in level at the break, with a goal out of nowhere. Lopez’s path to the box was blocked but the ball bounced loose to the midfielder and he quickly smashed a strike past Jan Oblak. Early in the second half Alvarez lobbed over the crossbar when running in on goal. The forward came to rue the miss when Barcelona took the lead. Yamal played a clever pass through Atletico’s defence and Lopez kept his cool to beat Oblak. It was his seventh league goal in 11 top flight appearances this season. Barcelona kept Atletico at bay well in the final stages to take three points home from the capital before the international break. Earlier on fourth-place Real Betis earned a 2-0 win at Elche, while Real Sociedad, fifth, defeated Rayo Vallecano 1-0. item.title: 2027 Elections: Lagos APC Candidate Hamzat Promises 4,000 CNG Buses, 77 Electric Ferries
item.description: The Lagos State governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Obafemi Hamzat, has promised to deploy 4,000 compressed natural gas (CNG) buses to move one million passengers daily as part of plans to ease transportation challenges in the state. Hamzat, the incumbent Deputy Governor, also disclosed plans to expand water transportation with 77 electric ferries and improve connectivity between different parts of Lagos through an integrated transport system. ﻿ He made the promises on Sunday during the Lagos governorship debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, The Cable, and Vanguard Newspaper. Explaining his transportation plans, Hamzat said the objective was to reduce commuting time and give residents more opportunities to rest and spend time with their families. “The plan is to give back time to the citizens to plan, to rest, to spend with their family. There’s nowhere in Africa that the private sector has funded a rail. “Since BRT started, it has done 77 million journeys; that is with 1,000 buses. My plan says we will push it to 4,000 buses; the idea is to move one million people a day with 4,000 CNG buses, meaning up to 5,000, create BRt lane from Marina to Epe, from Marina to Badagry and so on and so forth,” he said. “Today, over four million people have the Cowry card. What does that mean? It means you can use ferry, you can use rail, and you can use BRT buses — one payment — so that we can deal with how to subsidise it. On healthcare, the APC candidate promised to expand access to medical services by increasing the number of primary healthcare centres providing round-the-clock services. Hamzat said that out of the over 300 primary healthcare centres, the government planned to increase its flagship PHCs from 87 to 150, with the facilities operating 24 hours a day. He also disclosed that the state government was building more hospitals to improve healthcare access for residents. item.title: Seven killed, over 100 injured in Egypt train collision
item.description: At least seven people have been killed and more than 100 injured after two trains collided near Giza, Egypt, causing several carriages to derail and plunge down an embankment. The country’s railway authority said the trains, travelling south from Giza and Cairo, collided in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat. Egypt’s President, Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, said he had directed relevant authorities to investigate the circumstances surrounding the accident and ensure that anyone found negligent was held accountable. The public prosecutor’s office warned that the death toll could rise as rescue and recovery operations continued. The government said hospitals in the affected area had been placed on heightened alert to handle the large number of casualties. Health Minister, Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar, said victims were receiving treatment for various injuries, including broken bones and head injuries. The Egyptian Red Crescent also deployed personnel to provide emergency assistance and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene. The ministry confirmed that the driver of one of the trains was among those killed in the collision. According to reports, the first train was travelling from Giza to Fayoum when it crashed into the rear of another train heading from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks. Photographs from the scene showed several overturned carriages, with emergency responders and members of the public searching through the wreckage for survivors. Train services between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were deployed to remove the damaged trains. The railway authority had yet to announce when services would resume. The crash occurred close to the location of Egypt’s deadliest railway disaster, which happened in February 2002 when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor, killing more than 370 people officially, although some estimates put the death toll higher. Two other train accidents in the area in 2009 also claimed dozens of lives. The latest disaster sparked calls on Sunday for Egypt’s transport minister to resign over the recurring railway accidents. Meanwhile, foreign governments and diplomatic representatives expressed condolences and solidarity with Egypt over the tragedy. Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed solidarity with Egypt and wished the injured a speedy recovery. Turkey’s Ambassador to Egypt also conveyed his condolences on X to the victims, their families and the Egyptian people. item.title: No Political Will To Deal With Agberos In Lagos, Says NDC’s Funsho Doherty
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Lagos State, Funsho Doherty, has blamed the persistence of the agbero system in the state on a lack of political will by successive administrations to reform the transport sector. Agberos are transport touts who collect money from commercial bus drivers and other transport operators at motor parks, bus stops and along roads, often claiming to represent transport unions or park authorities. Speaking during the Lagos Governorship Debate on Sunday, Doherty said powerful interests within the existing transport system had made it difficult for successive governments to tackle the activities of the operators. The debate was organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, a coalition of five media organisations: Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard Newspapers. “Many of us understand this notion of the agbero system that people talk about. There is no political will to deal with that problem,” Doherty said. He argued that meaningful reform of public transportation would require a government that was accountable to residents rather than interests benefiting from the existing arrangement. “We will modernise the transportation system because we will be elected by the people, not by an agbero network,” he said. item.title: Idris inaugurates APC 2027 Campaign Council in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi Kebbi State Governor, Dr Nasir Idris, has inaugurated the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 Campaign Council, charging members to work towards securing victory for all party candidates in the forthcoming general elections. The governor inaugurated the council on Sunday at the Presidential Lodge, Birnin Kebbi, urging members to demonstrate commitment, dedication and determination in discharging their responsibilities. He described Kebbi as an APC stronghold and called on party stakeholders to return to their respective communities to mobilise support for the party’s candidates across all elective positions. Idris announced former Kebbi State Governor and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Turkey, Ambassador Saidu Usman Nasamu Dakingari, as chairman of the campaign council. “I have the honour and privilege of inaugurating this campaign council for the 2027 General Elections, which will be headed by the former Governor of Kebbi State and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Turkey, His Excellency, Ambassador Saidu Usman Nasamu Dakingari. I wish all members the very best of luck,” the governor said. Speaking at the event, the APC State Chairman, Alhaji Abubakar Kana-Zuru, commended Idris for his support for the party and commitment to the successful inauguration of the campaign council. He urged members to remain dedicated to campaign activities, work collectively and ensure the party’s success in the forthcoming elections. In his response, Dakingari thanked the governor for the confidence reposed in him and other members of the council. He assured the governor that the committee would work diligently and collectively to achieve the party’s objectives. “On behalf of all members of the committee, I assure you that we are fully committed to delivering on this assignment. We will work hard and put in our best to ensure the success of the APC in the 2027 General Elections,” he said. item.title: Police arrest six suspected phone thieves at Makinde’s Bauchi rally
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested six suspected phone thieves accused of stealing mobile phones from participants at the presidential campaign flag-off of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM) candidate, Governor Seyi Makinde, in the state. The suspects were arrested by operatives of the Police Violent Crimes Response Unit (VCRU), deployed to provide security at the campaign venue, following the detection of their suspicious movements during the event. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying exhibits were recovered from four of the suspects, while two others were identified by a victim as allegedly responsible for stealing his phone. The suspects were identified as Muhammad Rabiu, 20; Ibrahim Abubakar, 25; Hamza Usman, 18; Abba Bala, 20; Auwal Muhammad, 23; and Inusa Adamu, 20. Items recovered from them included an itel torchlight phone, an OPPO Android phone, an Infinix Smart 20 phone and a 20,000mAh power bank. The police spokesman said a Samsung Fold 4 allegedly stolen during the event had yet to be recovered, adding that efforts were being intensified to retrieve the device and other missing valuables. He said investigation was ongoing and that the suspects would be charged to court upon its conclusion. The Commissioner of Police, Sani-Omolori Aliyu, commended the operatives for their vigilance and prompt action, which led to the arrests and recovery of some stolen items. He warned criminal elements against exploiting public gatherings and political events to perpetrate crime, stressing that the command would not relent in its efforts to rid the state of criminal activities. The commissioner also urged members of the public attending political rallies and other public events to remain vigilant, safeguard their valuables and promptly report suspicious movements to security operatives. He called for continued public cooperation through the provision of timely and credible information to assist the command in preventing and controlling crime. item.title: Police rescue five kidnap victims, arrest three suspects in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has rescued five kidnapped victims and arrested three suspects following a coordinated security operation in Dakingari, Suru Local Government Area of the state. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman Kebbi, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the operation followed credible intelligence that armed men had invaded Dolen Kwandage Village and abducted three residents. The victims were identified as Samaila Abubakar, 35; Dayyaba Muhammadu, 32; and Balki Hakimi, 31. According to the statement, police operatives, working in collaboration with local vigilantes, swiftly mobilised to the area and pursued the assailants. The police said the superior firepower of the security team forced the kidnappers to abandon their captives, leading to the rescue of the three newly abducted residents and two other women who had earlier been held in captivity. The two women were identified as Moe Muddaha, 50, and Hadiza Bello, 30, both from Yarma Village in Suru LGA. All five victims were rescued unhurt and taken to the General Hospital, Dakingari, for medical examination before being reunited with their families. The operation also led to the arrest of three suspects identified as Umaru Janyo, 49, and Bube Kwaire, 28, both from Bendu Village, and Muhammadu Gyade, 22, of Tindifai Village. The police said other members of the criminal gang escaped with suspected gunshot injuries. Items recovered during the operation included an unregistered Haojue motorcycle, ₦308,000 in cash, a chain and a jerrycan. The command said it had intensified security patrols and surveillance in the area, adding that efforts were ongoing to track down the fleeing suspects and bring all those involved to justice. The Commissioner of Police, CP Umar M. Hadejia, commended the operatives and their local vigilante collaborators for their prompt response, courage and effective coordination. He reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting lives and property, disrupting criminal networks and ensuring that perpetrators of violent crimes were brought to justice. Hadejia also urged members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies to strengthen collective security efforts. item.title: 2027: Makinde backs state police, vows security overhaul
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has backed the establishment of state police, pledging to decentralise Nigeria’s security architecture if elected president in the 2027 general elections. Makinde stated this on Sunday during a live political programme on Jay FM 101.9 in Jos, Plateau State, where he outlined his proposed security reforms ahead of the party’s presidential campaign activities in the city. “I believe that we need to decentralise our security architecture. State police is one of the ways to achieve this, but it must be properly structured. “States that are ready should be allowed to establish their own police formations, while others can come on board when they are prepared,” he said. Recalling his engagement with former President Muhammadu Buhari on the issue in 2019, Makinde said the former president had expressed concerns about the ability of some states to fund their police formations. “When we approached President Buhari in 2019, one of the concerns he raised was that some states could not even pay workers’ salaries. He questioned how such states would be able to fund state police,” he said. Explaining the alternative adopted by governors in the South-West, Makinde said they settled for a regional security arrangement through Amotekun. He said the operatives gather intelligence and work with federal security agencies, adding that the initiative had helped improve security coordination in the region. The APM presidential candidate acknowledged concerns that state police could be abused by governors to intimidate political opponents and other citizens, but insisted that appropriate safeguards could address such risks. “We must not pretend that there are no concerns. Some people are worried that governors could use state police to oppress their opponents or intimidate citizens. Those concerns are valid, and we must put safeguards in place. “But the fact that something can be abused does not mean we should not do it. We must design a system that ensures accountability and protects the rights of the people,” he said. On the pace of implementation, Makinde said states should be allowed to establish their police formations at different times, depending on their readiness and capacity. He cited Nigeria’s transition to self-government and independence as an example of how states could adopt the arrangement at different paces. “We had self-government in 1957 and independence in 1960. We did not achieve everything at once. In the same way, states can move at different paces,” he said. Makinde also warned that Nigeria’s growing population, particularly its large youth population, required urgent government attention through job creation and opportunities for economic advancement. “We are talking about a country that could have a population of over 300 million people, with more than 70 per cent below the age of 34. item.title: Lagos 2027: PDP’s Deji Doherty Defends Alliance With Wike, Tinubu
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has defended his political relationship with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, despite the latter’s support for President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress (APC). Doherty said Wike’s position in the APC-led Federal Government does not make him an enemy of democracy, arguing that politics and democracy can accommodate different political alignments. He spoke during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, Vanguard Newspapers and The Cable on Sunday. Responding to a question on how he could offer a genuine opposition alternative in Lagos despite emerging from a PDP faction loyal to Wike, Doherty said his candidacy was the product of 26 years of political work and grassroots support. “My emergence in the People’s Democratic Party is out of 26 years of hard work, consistency, determination, and continued support for the grassroots. I have built a grassroots structure right from scratch, and I know there are a lot of people here that can testify to that. That’s number one. “Number two is that Nyesom Wike is our leader. He’s our national leader. He will continue to be my leader, and he will continue to show us that politics and democracy are not enemies,” he said. The PDP candidate further defended Wike’s relationship with the President, pointing to what he described as benefits from the Federal Government. “Once we are getting results from the FCT, we are getting results from Mr. President, we are getting monies into the pockets of governors in different states,” Doherty added. item.title: Lagos 2027: Rhodes-Vivour, Hamzat, Doherty unveil plans on housing, transport, others
item.description: Governorship candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), All Progressives Congress (APC), Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) have presented their proposals for addressing some of Lagos State’s major challenges, including housing, transportation, and healthcare, ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The candidates made their positions known during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Vanguard Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, and The Cable on Sunday. Housing The ADC candidate, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, promised to deliver more than 100,000 housing units if elected, saying his administration would prioritise affordable accommodation for ordinary residents rather than the wealthy. He said the proposed houses would be allocated transparently to prevent individuals from acquiring multiple units under the scheme. “The elites, the rich, can do it for themselves. The government’s role is to lift up people that cannot do it for themselves, and this comes into housing to ensure that we deliver 100,000-plus housing units and make it affordable so that it is transparently allocatable. We are not going to have a situation where one person can own ten units,” Rhodes-Vivour said. The ADC candidate also promised legislation to protect tenants against arbitrary rent increases, proposing that landlords should give at least six months’ notice before increasing rents, with the increment guided by a stipulated percentage. He added that a feedback mechanism would be established to enable tenants to report landlords who violated the proposed regulations, assuring that offenders would be brought to justice. The All Progressives Congress candidate, Obafemi Hamzat, who is the incumbent deputy governor, pledged to enforce existing regulations against arbitrary rent increases and the demand for multiple years’ rent in advance. Hamzat said his administration would ensure compliance with the Lagos State Real Estate Registration Agency Law, stressing that tenants should not be required to pay two or three years’ rent upfront. “The next chapter for Lagos is to enforce. To make sure people are not asked two or three years ahead, because people don’t get paid two or three years ahead,” he said. He also said the state had established 24 housing estates in the last eight years, promising to expand access to quality accommodation through increased mortgage facilities and the completion of ongoing housing projects across the state. The NDC candidate, Funsho Doherty, called for greater government involvement in providing affordable housing, arguing that private developers alone could not meet the accommodation needs of low- and middle-income residents. He also proposed the establishment of an ombudsman’s office to address what he described as exploitation of tenants through excessive agency, legal and other charges. item.title: ‘That’s not going to happen’ – Carrick rules out resigning as Man United boss
item.description: Michael Carrick said he expects to “move forward and keep working” as Manchester United manager despite dropping into the Premier League relegation zone. United twice came from two goals down to salvage a remarkable 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday. Goals in stoppage time from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point and potentially gave Carrick a stay of execution ahead of a two-week international break. “We haven’t won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on the things that we’ve been working on,” Carrick told Sky Sports. “Showing a lot of the good (things) in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.” Results this weekend dropped United into the bottom three after August for the first time in 40 years. “We’re in November,” added Carrick. “I don’t like the situation where we are, I don’t like the results that we’ve had, but we can definitely do something about it.” The former United midfielder dismissed any suggestion he could resign if it was in the best interests of the club and said he would not seek out discussions with his superiors on where his future lies. “That’s not going to happen,” said Carrick when asked if he would resign. “I’m quite clear what direction the club needs to go in, and we’ve just got to win games.” The 45-year-old added: “I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there… as a normal international week is, we’ll have some training, we’ll have one or two days off, not too much, but we’ll train and get ready for the next game.” United travel to rivals Liverpool when they are next in action on November 22. item.title: VIDEO: Lagos Debt Burden Weighing State Down, Says PDP’s Deji Doherty
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Lagos State, Adedeji Doherty, has criticised the state’s debt burden, saying it is weighing down the economy. Doherty said this during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, Vanguard Newspapers and The Cable on Sunday. He said Lagos spends close to 19 billion to 20 billion on servicing its external and domestic debts, describing the burden as heavy. “The debt burden (in Lagos) is heavy. When you are paying close to about 19 to 20 billion in external debt, in domestic debt, in foreign debt then you have a burden you are carrying that is weighing you down,” he said. The PDP candidate also faulted what he described as the lack of independence of local government areas, arguing that they are closest to the people and should have the resources to meet their needs. “When your LGAs are not independent, those are the closest to the people and when you do not give them what they need, when you are taking in LASAA and putting it in the pocket of the state, these are the issues,” he added. ﻿ The post VIDEO: Lagos Debt Burden Weighing State Down, Says PDP’s Deji Doherty appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027: We Will Make Education Truly Free In Lagos – NDC’s Funsho Doherty
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Funsho Doherty, has promised to make education completely free in Lagos State if elected in 2027. Doherty made the promise during the 2027 Lagos State governorship debate organised by Channels Television, TVC, Punch Newspapers, Vanguard Newspapers and The Cable on Sunday. He said his administration would focus on improving the lives of residents by equipping them with education and relevant skills. “So, our policies are aimed at capacitating the people, giving them skills, ensuring that there is no child born in Lagos who does not get an education because their parents cannot afford it. We have said we will make education truly free, not nominally free. Truly free, so people will not pay exam fees, they will not be asked to come and pay taxes at a point when they have to write their exams,” Doherty said. He also promised to introduce a programme that would provide children in public schools with one affordable meal every day.
